source.title: RL Excursions during Pre-Training: Re-examining Policy Optimization for LLM training
source.authors: Rachit Bansal; Clara Mohri; Tian Qin; David Alvarez-Melis; S. Kakade

record.tranche_reason: The study examines reinforcement learning and downstream math performance, but does not test held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling laws, extrapolation of loss fits, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream pass@k outcomes for RL and SFT across pretraining checkpoints, model sizes, and data compositions. These are not held-out cross-entropy loss measurements or tests of the stated scaling-law versions. Figure 5 does report a relationship between base-model pass@k and post-RL pass@k; this is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study applies RL and SFT to pretraining checkpoints of 1B and 4B OLMo2-style models and reports downstream math pass@k. It measures no held-out pretraining loss and fits no power laws. It does not test extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, model shape, or whether downstream scaling is predictable. Chinchilla appears only as a reference point (pretraining on '∼2.5× Chinchilla optimal tokens', RL gains 'before Chinchilla optimal'), not as something tested.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares RL and supervised fine-tuning recipes rather than reproducing or evaluating the scaling-law methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported base-to-post-RL relationship is examined across GSM8K and MATH, pass@1 and pass@32, and multiple pre-training regimes; no scaling-law fit sensitivity is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model 8-shot test pass@k shows a generally monotonic increasing relationship with post-RL pass@k across checkpoints and pretraining regimes (GSM8K; MATH at 1B/50B, 1B/60B, 4B/50B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Base-model pass@k predicts the downstream outcome of direct RL.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling model size from 1B to 4B raises base MATH accuracy but not the RL gain over base. Adding 10B math tokens (1B/60B) substantially raises the RL gain (Fig 4, §3.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data composition matters more than model size for the gains from RL post-training.

record.problems: The paper reports the relevant pass@k relationships graphically without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. Its experiments are limited to 1B and 4B models and 50–60B pre-training tokens, but it does not provide evidence on the claim's loss-scaling outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the study's model-size and data-composition comparisons: those report changes in downstream RL gains rather than any version's named loss-scaling or compute-allocation measure.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute is reported.
No compute-matched N/D allocation is tested. Chinchilla-optimal token count is used only as a landmark.
No depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit for RL, fine-tuning or other modalities. The RL rollout study (App. D) compares FLOP efficiency of n=5 vs n=64 without any scaling-law form.

Base accuracy rises across pretraining tokens and is higher at 4B than 1B (Figs 2, 4, 9–11). No predictability claim, fit, or loss–downstream relation is reported. Fig 5 relates base pass@k to post-RL pass@k, not to scale or loss.
No exponents or fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': scaling laws are invoked only as a Chinchilla-optimal token landmark. All rows correctly link to 'none'. Their 'observed' states describe the study's own finding, not any version. Scale-related observations (base accuracy rising with tokens and with N) are descriptive downstream curves with no fit or predictability analysis, so they are not counted for V6.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run loss fits are extrapolated to larger runs.
No compute-matched parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal scaling is evaluated.
No architecture-depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count is reported.
No other modality, repeated-data regime, or transfer/fine-tuning power-law test is reported.
The study relates base pass@k to post-RL pass@k, not downstream performance to scale or pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents, fit choices, or bending of loss curves are examined.
